amendments.rule:
The **substantival article** — `הַ` on a participle or adjective used as a noun — takes the pronoun the ASV supplies to make it substantival, and heads on that pronoun rather than on the relative that follows it. `הָרַע` → *that which was evil* is the article with *that which*, headed on *that*; `הָעֹשֶׂה` → *him that doeth* is the article with *him that*, headed on *him*. The supplied pronoun is the article's own rendering and is never `added`. The predicate word keeps its own English, including any copula the ASV supplies, which stays with it under rule 20: in *that which is right*, *is* and *right* belong to the adjective and only *that which* belongs to the article. **An attributive article the ASV renders by a relative goes the same way.** Where `הַ` stands on a participle or adjective modifying an explicit noun and the ASV writes a relative instead of a *the* — `אֹיְבֶיךָ הַקָּמִים עָלֶיךָ` → *thine enemies that rise up against thee*, `הָאִישׁ הָרַךְ` → *The man that is tender*, `הַכְּתוּבִים` → *that are written* — the article takes that relative and heads on it, while the participle or adjective keeps its own English together with any supplied copula, exactly as above. **A demonstrative or possessive determiner the ASV writes in the article's place goes the same way, whatever the article stands on.** Where the ASV writes no *the* for the phrase but a *this*, *that*, *these*, *those*, or a possessive *his*, *her*, *thy*, *thine*, standing where the phrase's *the* would stand — `הַזִּמָּה` → *this lewdness*, `הַגְּדֹלוֹת` → *thine elder* — that word is what the ASV has written for the article: the article takes it and heads on it, and it is neither `added` nor a reason to mark the article `unrepresented`. **Read that as no *the* standing before the article's own word, not as no *the* anywhere in the phrase.** Where the article sits on the *nomen rectum* of a construct chain and the ASV writes a *the* before the construct and a demonstrative or possessive before the rectum's own word, rule 29's arthrous case governs the count: nothing is fronted, the article takes the determiner standing before its own word, and the construct takes the supplied *the*. `יְמֵי הַמִּשְׁתֶּה` → *the days of* ***their*** *feasting* gives *their* to the article and *the days* to the construct, exactly as `שְׂדֵה הָעִיר` → *the fields of the city* gives the second *the* to the article there. Do not mark such an article `unrepresented` and the determiner `added` under rule 18's closing sentence: that sentence governs a supplied possessive with no determiner morpheme standing before the word it determines, and here one does. **But only where no other morpheme licenses that determiner.** A pronominal suffix standing in the same phrase is rendered by a possessive of its own under rule 18, and where the ASV writes one determiner for the whole phrase the suffix takes it and the article is `unrepresented`: `אֲחוֹתֵךְ הַגְּדוֹלָה` → *thine elder sister* gives *thine* to the suffix on `אָחוֹת` and leaves the article nothing, while `אֲחוֹתַיִךְ הַגְּדֹלוֹת` → *thy sisters, thine elder sisters* writes a determiner for each and the article takes the second; so too `אֲחִיהֶם הַבְּכוֹר` → *their eldest brother's*, where the suffix takes *their* and the article has nothing. Count the determiners and read which word each stands before, as rule 29 counts the ASV's *the*s. Read what the ASV writes for the article and let that decide which rule governs: a bare *the* is rule 15's ordinary attributive article, a relative or a supplied pronoun is this rule's, a demonstrative or possessive determiner is this rule's too, and where the ASV writes none of them the article is `unrepresented` under rule 29. Where coordinated attributives share a single written relative, the first article takes it and the rest are `unrepresented` under rules 22 and 47.

**An articleless attributive that the ASV recasts as a relative clause keeps the supplied relative with the attributive itself.** Where an adjective or participle without an article modifies an explicit noun and the ASV writes a relative frame — `אֲדָמָה טְמֵאָה` → *a land that is unclean* — the attributive takes the relative together with its own English and any copula rule 20 supplies, headed on the word carrying its lexeme. The relative realizes the Hebrew attributive relation and is not `added`; rule 55's supplied clause subordinator is a different construction.
amendments.why: Rule 41's possessive-determiner clause is conditioned on the ASV writing *no* `the` for the phrase. JOB.1.5's `יְמֵי הַמִּשְׁתֶּה` → *the days of their feasting* writes one — before the construct — and a possessive before the article's own word, so the clause does not reach the case on its literal wording, even though rule 29's arthrous-rectum clause counts the determiners exactly this way and rule 41's own closing sentence directs the reader to count them. Left unamended, a later pass could mark the article `unrepresented` and the *their* `added` under rule 18's closing sentence, which is the reading rule 41 exists to rule out. The corpus supports the underlying treatment without contradiction: `הַ` aligns to a possessive in 31 units (*his* 15, *their* 6, *her* 6, *thy* 4) across the finished chapters, and rule 29 already records `שְׂדֵה הָעִיר` → *the fields of the city* as the arthrous count this extends. The amendment narrows nothing: the suffix limit, the determiner count and the articleless-attributive paragraph are carried through unchanged, and the JOB.1.13/18 `אֲחִיהֶם הַבְּכוֹר` case is added as a worked example of that limit.

conventions: The apodosis waw of a וַיְהִי frame may open the following verse. In JOB.1.13–14 the frame begins at וַיְהִי הַיּוֹם (13) and its apodosis is וּמַלְאָךְ בָּא (14), so JOB.1.13's verb takes only *it fell* with no complementizer to place, and JOB.1.14's opening וּ takes *that* rather than *and* under rules 45 and 14. The chapter's other three frames (vv. 5, 6 and the same 13) keep the *that* on the apodosis waw within their own verse. Do not give a frame's *that* to הָיָה anywhere in this chapter.

The messenger's refrain of vv. 15, 16, 17 and 19 is aligned identically in all four: the waw of וָאִמָּלְטָה takes *and*; the Niphal takes *am escaped*, headed on the participle; its paragogic he is its own `unrepresented` unit (rule 32); רַק takes *only* and the explicit אֲנִי takes *I*; לְבַדִּי is one three-morpheme unit rendered *alone* (rule 30); and in לְהַגִּיד לָךְ the first לְ takes *to*, the infinitive *tell*, the second לְ is `unrepresented` because the ASV writes a bare English object (rule 40), and its suffix takes *thee*. Align any further occurrence the same way rather than re-deriving it.

Verses 16, 17 and 18 all read *While he was yet speaking* but do not carry the same source. Verses 16 and 17 write the adverb עוֹד, which takes *yet*, and the supplied subordinator *While* is `added` under rule 55, the two English words being separated by *he was* and so failing rule 55's contiguity test. Verse 18 writes the preposition עַד instead, which takes *While* under rule 52's temporal case, and there the intensifier *yet* is the word no morpheme answers to and is `added`. The differing `added` token across these three verses is deliberate; read which of עוֹד or עַד is written before placing either word.

Multi-morpheme expressions in this chapter were fused or split by rule 30's one-English-rendering subtraction test, not by lemma. Fused as single units: מֵאַיִן → *Whence*, בְּתוֹךְ → *among*, שִׂים לֵב → *considered*, וְאוּלָם → *But*, אִם־לֹא → *and*, מֵעִם → *from*, עַל־יְדֵי → *beside*, מֵעֵבֶר → *from*, לְבַדִּי → *alone*, שָׁמָּה → *thither*, כָּל־הַיָּמִים → *continually*, וְלֹא → *nor*. Split under rule 2 because each morpheme keeps an English word of its own: מִסָּבִיב → *on* + *every side*, and לְפִי־חָרֶב → *with* + *the edge* + *of the sword*. A compound preposition whose second morpheme has no separate English word fuses here; one whose object is rendered by a content noun does not.

report: Checked all 46 candidate lemma groups, the four `added` units the lemma table cannot see (v15 *upon them*, v16 *While*, v17 *While*, v18 *yet*), and every verse end to end. No construction is analysed two ways with nothing in the source to license the difference, so patches is empty.

The presentative וַיְהִי frame is uniform across vv. 5, 6, 13 and 14: the complementizer always goes to the apodosis waw under rule 45, and the verb keeps only *it was so* / *it came to pass* / *it fell*. In vv. 13–14 that apodosis waw is the next verse's opening וּ, which is why JOB.1.13 places no *that* and JOB.1.14 opens with *that* rather than *and*.

The vv. 16–18 refrain looks like a split in English and is not. Verses 16 and 17 write the adverb עוֹד, which takes *yet*, leaving the supplied *While* `added`; verse 18 writes the preposition עַד, which takes *While*, leaving the supplied *yet* `added`. Each verse ran rule 55's count against a different source, so the differing `added` token is licensed.

Article placement follows a different clause of rule 29 in each phrase because the ASV writes a different number of *the*s: בְּנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים (v6) fronts the rectum's article; אַרְבַּע פִּנּוֹת הַבַּיִת (v19) renders the rectum arthrously, so nothing is fronted and the determiner before *four* is supplied; בְּנֵי קֶדֶם (v3) has no article morpheme at all. הַשָּׂטָן's article is unrepresented in all seven occurrences.

Fusion under rule 30 is drawn by the one-English-rendering subtraction test rather than by lemma: מֵאַיִן, בְּתוֹךְ, שִׂים לֵב, וְאוּלָם, אִם־לֹא, מֵעִם, עַל־יְדֵי, מֵעֵבֶר, לְבַדִּי, שָׁמָּה, כָּל־הַיָּמִים and וְלֹא fuse, while מִסָּבִיב → *on every side* and לְפִי־חָרֶב → *with the edge of the sword* split, because there each morpheme keeps an English word of its own. That line is consistent chapter-wide.

BSB: no genuine error among the 29 disagreements. They are the documented convention families — 15 articles the ASV writes no *the* for, 9 prepositions an ASV recasting leaves nothing to say (rule 40), 4 paragogic *he* (rule 32), and the ךָ of לִבְּךָ absorbed into the fused שִׂים לֵב → *considered* (rules 30, 22). BSB attaches each to its host word; that is a convention difference, not a correction. No accepted edge was changed.

Observation only, no edge changed: JOB.1.19's note for s013 calls אַרְבַּע the "outer construct" where MACULA tags it Acfsa, absolute. The edge and the supplied *the* are placed correctly under rules 15 and 29 either way; only the note's label is loose.
